findings.title: Unicode alias restoration skips retained extension attributes
findings.suggested_fix: Stop applying aliases to every XML attribute/text token, or restore aliases in all moddle-owned storage including $attrs and other $-prefixed opaque fields. Prefer an XML-aware adapter that aliases only actual ID and modeled IDREF/QName values, then add an imported-extension round-trip test proving unknown attributes remain byte-semantically unchanged.

findings.title: The hand-maintained document ID visitor already omits local ID references
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the generic-properties special case with one typed, exhaustive visitor shared by validation and serialization. At minimum include boundary attachTo, dataObjectRef/itemSubjectRef, and multiInstance.loopDataInputRef/loopDataOutputRef alongside eventDefinitionPayload, and table-test every emitted local ID reference.

findings.title: Invalid-ID discovery depends on moddle's partial elementsById index
findings.suggested_fix: Collect and validate authored id attributes with an XML-aware scanner before invoking moddle, retaining element paths/locations for diagnostics. Do not use elementsById as the discovery mechanism: moddle omits elements whose IDs fail its own lexical check, so validator behavior changes with moddle internals.

residual_risks: The Unicode compatibility layer remains coupled to undocumented bpmn-moddle object-graph details and to moddle-xml's current ASCII ID behavior, so dependency upgrades can silently change which aliases or IDs need adaptation.
testing_gaps: No test imports and reserializes a valid Unicode ID that is also used in an unknown extension attribute; the current adapter emits the generated ASCII alias from $attrs.
The document-ID table does not exercise attachTo, dataObjectRef/itemSubjectRef, or multi-instance input/output references through direct serializer ingress.

Import and validator tests cover colon but not leading digit/dash/dot, whitespace, out-of-range supplementary characters, or malformed surrogates end to end; moddle drops several of these from elementsById and only produces a generic unparsable-content warning.
